To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an improved analytical description of the horizon-absorped gravitational-wave energy flux for small bodies in circular orbits in the equatorial plan of a Kerr black holes, which agrees with the numerical results up to the light-ring frequency and reproduces the expected behavior of the flux at the horizon frequency and close to the light-ring.

we propose an analytical model for the absorption flux of small circular orbits around a Kerr black hole which agrees with numerical simulations and which captures the presence of a divergence at the light ring.
We construct an improved model for the gravitational-wave absorption flux of a small mass in circular orbit in Kerr spacetime that reproduces numerical data with high accuracy.

the modeling and simulation of the gravitational radiation emitted by compact binary systems in general relativity.
the modeling and simulation of gravitational waveforms emitted by a small body orbiting a spinning black hole, in the context of the post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity.
the modeling of the gravitational-wave emission in the strong-field regime.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new analytical model of the horizon-absorped gravitational-wave energy flux that agrees well with numerical data and that can be extended to the merger of small mass-rati binary systems.
we propose a simple, yet accurate, model for the absorption flux of a small mass in a circular orbit around a Kerr black hole, and we provide a simple method to improve the accuracy of PN fluxes.
the proposed absorption flux model is more accurate than the PN flux model and can be used to replace the latter in the modeling of the gravitational-wave signal of small-mass-ratio binary systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mode-by-mode analysis is a useful tool for modeling horizon absorption in black hole spacetimes.
the PN flux is not a good model for the absorbed flux in the strong-field regime of Kerr spacetime.
a simple model for the horizon absorption flux can be constructed from a mode-by-mode analysis of the flux, which can be compared with numerical results for a wide range of Kerr spins.
